## Overview of Zscaler’s Zero-Day Support for Apple Ecosystem

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/Articles/aSmPJ00000D9zuU0AR/overview-of-zscalers-zeroday-support-for-apple-ecosystem
- Type: Article
- Last activity: 2025-06-03T16:18:30.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Article Details

Client Connector

DEEPAK G

(Employee) posted an Article

June 3, 2025 at 4:18 PM

Overview of Zscaler’s Zero-Day Support for Apple Ecosystem

About Zscaler’s Zero-Day Support (ZDS) for Apple Ecosystem:

In today’s fast-moving digital era, staying ahead of technological upgrades is no longer optional, it’s essential. With Apple annually releasing new hardware and software offerings across iOS, iPadOS, and macOS, enterprises face twin challenges of adopting these advancements without disruption and ensuring security.

This is where Zscaler’s ZDS plays a pivotal role in facilitating a seamless, secure, and enterprise-ready Apple enterprise adoption.

Key Cornerstones of Zscaler’s ZDS for Apple Ecosystem:

Apple ZDS is Zscaler’s commitment to ensuring that Zscaler’s flagship endpoint security solution Zscaler Client Connector is fully compatible with Apple’s latest operating systems and hardware on the day they are launched by Apple.

This critical support is the result of rigor, and relentless focus involving Zscaler & Apple’s Joint Alignment towards:

Driving Seamless Deployments:

Product, engineering, and field teams combine forces to deliver one clear objective: delivering stress-free seamless transitions for Zscaler customers deploying Zscaler on Apple devices.

Rigorous Beta Testing to Ensure Compatibility:

Zscaler collaborates with Apple during its beta and pre-release cycles, ensuring seamless compatibility across iOS, iPadOS, macOS and Apple (silicon) hardware before launch day. It provides the outcome of the test results as Knowledge Base articles and facilitates discussions around them in the Zenith Community offering complete transparency and visibility to increase the customer confidence in adopting Zscaler on the latest Apple releases.

Continuous Community Engagement:

Zscaler will continuously share the results of its beta testing with the Zenith Community to allow Zscaler customers to voice their concerns and share test results for their own use cases.

This plays a major role in ensuring:

Immediate Compatibility:

Enterprises can seamlessly upgrade to the newest Apple devices and operating systems without worrying about compatibility issues and downtime.

As bugs are reported by Zscaler customers in seed releases, Zscaler will work to resolve them if it is at its end before the respective operating system (OS) version is released in General Availability (GA).

On the other hand, if the issue lies on the Apple side, Zscaler will provide a list of known issues when the new OS is released to ensure that the Zscaler customers are made aware of them prior to upgrading.

Disruption-Free Innovation:

Zero-day readiness ensures that the productivity of Zscaler Customers isn’t hindered by tech transitions and downtime thereby unlocking the full potential of Apple’s latest releases from day one.

Drive End User Confidence:

Provides the much-needed confidence for the customer to make an upgrade decision of their Zscaler products on Apple devices by reviewing the Beta testing results.

Zscaler’s Commitment towards ZDS for Apple Ecosystem:

Zscaler is fully committed towards:

Ensuring that enterprises confidently adopt the latest Apple innovations without fear of downtime, disruptions, or vulnerabilities.

Setting new benchmarks for excellence in secure digital transformation.

Translating these commitments to reality underpins Zscaler’s transformative role in modern enterprise security. Achieving ZDS would also act as a testament to Zscaler’s dedication to winning its customer trust.

Zscaler’s ZDS Roadmap for Apple Ecosystem:

As part of this journey, Zscaler strives to partner closely with Apple, aligning its products, engineering, partnership, and customer facing field teams with Apple’s release cycles.

Zscaler’s ZDS roadmap includes:

Launching synchronized product updates that match Apple’s releases.

Building environments to support real-time internal testing on Apple Beta infrastructure.

Showcasing readiness through blogs, knowledge base & community articles, and dedicated Apple beta corners in its community forums.

Through these efforts, Zscaler strives to bring Zero-Day Support to life, step by step, with the same customer-first mindset that had defined it all along.

Zscaler’s ZDS for Apple Ecosystem- Zenith Community Engagement:

Zscaler welcomes its customers and stakeholders to share the challenges they face across Apple device rollouts apart from their feedback & inputs on what excites them most about same-day compatibility and the problems that it would help them solve by creating a thread in the

Apple ZDS Corner

We encourage them to post specific questions and suggestions on this topic in the comments section of this article.

## How to Deploy Zscaler Client Connector (ZCC) on Android Devices Using Intune

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/Articles/aSmPJ00000EQ69l0AD/how-to-deploy-zscaler-client-connector-zcc-on-android-devices-using-intune
- Type: Article
- Last activity: 2025-07-25T17:02:56.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Article Details

FloZSupport

(Employee) posted an Article

Edited July 25, 2025 at 5:02 PM

How to Deploy Zscaler Client Connector (ZCC) on Android Devices Using Intune

Disclaimer:

This information is provided as-is for the benefit of the Community.

Please contact

Zscaler Professional Services

if you require assistance with your specific environment.

With special thanks to

Anurag Kesar

for submitting this guide!

***

There is no direct support for configuring ZCC as a VPN profile on Android devices in Intune. This is different from iOS, where profiles can be set up.

Key Findings from Microsoft Documentation

VPN and Per-App VPN Policy on Android

(Microsoft article)

Android VPN client configurations in Intune are managed via App Configuration Policies, not VPN profiles.

The officially supported VPN clients for per-app VPN in Intune include:

Cisco AnyConnect

Citrix SSO

F5 Access

Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect

Pulse Secure

SonicWall Mobile Connect

Note:

Zscaler Client Connector (ZCC) is not included in the list of supported VPN clients for per-app VPN settings in Intune.

VPN Profiles for Android Enterprise Devices

(Microsoft article)

Intune permits VPN profiles for certain Android Enterprise devices, but supported VPN connection types include

Cisco AnyConnect

SonicWall Mobile Connect

F5 Access

Pulse Secure

Microsoft Tunnel

Note:

ZCC is not an option for creating VPN profiles in Intune for Android devices.

Always-on VPN requires using a supported VPN client, which does not currently include ZCC.

Next Steps and Alternatives

Since ZCC is not natively supported for VPN profiles on Android in Intune, a different approach is recommended:

Deploy ZCC using Intune App Configuration Policies for Android devices.

To simplify the process for users, enable Single Sign-On (SSO) by setting up ZCC as the Identity Provider (IDP). This prevents users from needing to manually enter credentials or go through enrollment pages.

Additional Information

For step-by-step guidance, refer to this resource on deploying

ZCC with Microsoft Intune on Android devices

## Health Metrics (ZCC Telemetry) Enablement Announcement

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/Articles/aSmPJ00000EQryN0AT/health-metrics-zcc-telemetry-enablement-announcement
- Type: Article
- Last activity: 2025-07-25T21:10:49.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Article Details

FloZSupport

(Employee) posted an Article

Edited July 25, 2025 at 9:10 PM

Health Metrics (ZCC Telemetry) Enablement Announcement

1. What is ZCC Telemetry?

ZCC Telemetry is a new feature designed to improve Zscaler Client Connector (ZCC) supportability by collecting telemetry and device event information. This feature provides data that ZDX already collects, specifically for customers who do not currently use ZDX. This enables enhanced reporting and proactive issue detection capabilities.

2. What types of events does ZCC Telemetry collect?

ZCC Telemetry collects data related to various device events, including:

Crash events

End-user interactions and notifications

PAC-related issues

System events (network, OS, and power-related data)

This data helps improve insight into device health and operations.

3. How does ZCC Telemetry benefit customers?

ZCC Telemetry enhances reporting in the Client Connector Portal by providing valuable insights, such as:

OTP (One-Time-Password) usage reporting

Posture check failures

Service enabling/disabling activity by users

Customers gain better visibility into device and user behavior without the need for ZDX, this helps with improved troubleshooting and diagnostics as well.

4. Is any personal identifiable information (PII) collected or processed?

ZCC telemetry collection of PII, such as network adapter Service Set Identifier (SSID) and IPv6 addresses, is governed by the existing Mobile Administration fields Under

Administration > Client Connector Support > User Privacy

: `Collect Device Owner Information` and `Collect Machine Hostname Information`. These toggles can be configured to prevent ZCC telemetry from collecting these specific details. All other information gathered by ZCC telemetry is not classified as PII.

5. How is ZCC Telemetry data stored and secured to ensure compliance with data privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR)?

Data for organizations in the EU and AU are stored in their respective regional clusters.

6. Who is impacted by this?

This change applies to all customer tenants currently using ZCC for Windows and macOS. For customer tenants that already use ZDX, only devices within those tenants not currently using ZDX will get the ZCC Telemetry module enabled.

7. Will this change impact the user experience?

No, ZCC Telemetry’s activation does not alter the user experience. Additionally, the ZDX module remains hidden in the ZCC interface.

8. When will ZCC Telemetry be rolled out?

Zscaler will enable ZCC Telemetry incrementally for tenants beginning on August 8, 2025. The rollout will conclude by February 28, 2026.

9. How will I know that ZCC Telemetry is now active in my tenant?

If ZCC telemetry is enabled for an organization, the “Health Metrics” toggle will appear in the app profile, indicating that ZCC telemetry is active.

10. Why is Zscaler introducing ZCC Telemetry now?

This initiative is part of an effort to improve observability and supportability for ZCC deployments. ZCC Telemetry allows for most device issues to be detected, debugged, and resolved without manually retrieving and analyzing log files, significantly accelerating issue resolution times.

11. What happens if my tenant does not have ZDX, will I get access to some ZDX dashboards or only dashboards in the Client Connector Portal?

Even without ZDX, ZCC Telemetry will still collect events. While the ZDX Administration Portal and dashboards won't be accessible, some of these events will be visible in the Client Connector Portal, as detailed in the

advisory

12. Can I Opt Out of ZCC Telemetry?

ZCC telemetry can be disabled through the Mobile Administration Portal. This option becomes available in the App profile only after the feature is enabled for an organization. If the toggle is not visible in Mobile Administration Portal, it indicates that the feature has not yet been enabled for that organization.

13. Does enabling ZCC Telemetry require a separate license or subscription fee?

No, Zscaler will enable it as a backend control. ZCC Telemetry will then be automatically rolled out to eligible devices i.e. Windows ZCC 4.6+ and Mac ZCC 4.5.1+.

14. Will enabling ZCC Telemetry limit or affect my ability to upgrade to ZDX in the future?

ZDX takes precedence over ZCC telemetry. If ZDX is already deployed on a device, enabling ZCC telemetry will not override ZDX. Conversely, if ZCC telemetry is enabled on a device, deploying ZDX will override ZCC telemetry and install ZDX on that device.

15. Does enabling ZCC Telemetry require updating to a specific ZCC version?

The minimum supported ZCC versions for telemetry are Windows ZCC 4.6 and Mac ZCC 4.5.1. Older versions of ZCC will not be impacted.

16. Will ZCC Telemetry result in changes to device performance or resource usage (e.g., CPU/memory impact)?

Enabling ZCC telemetry installs the ZCC telemetry module as a Windows service on the device. ZCC Telemetry offers a streamlined version of ZDX, specifically designed for customers and devices who do not currently utilize ZDX. It gathers a subset of the data that ZDX typically collects, resulting in lower CPU and memory consumption compared to enabling ZDX on the device. If non ZDX customers haven't allowed the ZSAUpm process as per the

recommended processes to be allowed

, customers must allow this process now for ZCC telemetry to properly work.

17. What specific dashboards or reports will be enabled with ZCC Telemetry?

ZCC telemetry enables Device Event collection, which drives some recent reporting improvements in the Client Connector Portal, including reporting for OTP usage, Posture failures and Service Enabling/Disabling by users. Tenants without ZDX or ZCC Telemetry will not have access to these dashboards.

18. If I am already using ZDX, does ZCC Telemetry provide any additional value beyond what I already have?

Events collected as part of ZCC telemetry are also collected by ZDX. So customers receive the benefits of ZCC telemetry if they have ZDX.

ZCC telemetry is primarily for non ZDX devices. However, devices already with ZDX will have access to the Client Connector Portal dashboards.

19. Are there differences in event collection between ZCC Telemetry and the ZDX Standard/Advanced tiers?

No, ZCC telemetry data is a subset of the data collected from devices with Standard/Advanced licenses.

Zscaler Now Supports Apple macOS Tahoe and iOS 26 on Day One!

Zscaler is proud to announce that

we have achieved zero-day compatibility

with Apple’s newly released macOS Tahoe and iOS 26, ensuring that the latest supported

Zscaler Client Connector *releases are fully compatible with macOS Tahoe and iOS 26 from the moment they went live.

This has essentially paved for Zscaler Customers to take advantage of new Apple product releases as soon as they become available on the market.

The following *releases have been tested and supported with new Operating Systems

Apple OS

Supported Zscaler Client Connector Releases

macOS Tahoe

v4.5.2,

v4.5 and v4.3.1 (LTS)

iOS 26

v4.3.5

Zscaler’s Apple Zero Day Support: About

Apple ZDS is Zscaler’s commitment towards a seamless, secure, and enterprise-ready Apple enterprise adoption by ensuring its flagship endpoint security solution Zscaler Client Connector is fully compatible with Apple’s latest operating systems and hardware on the day they are launched by Apple.

Zscaler’s Apple Zero Day Support: Key Outcome Drivers for Customers

Zscaler’s collaboration with Apple through the AppleSeed for IT program means Zscaler is not just prepared but rather fully aligned with Apple’s vision.

This ensures that Zscaler Customers benefit from this strategic alliance with secure, reliable and future-proof product experience.

This critical milestone underscores Zscaler and Apple’s joint alignment towards empowering its valued customer with:

Immediate Compatibility and Seamless Transition to Latest Operating System:

On the day Apple releases a new iOS or macOS version, its customer’s workforce is already covered! No downtime, no uncertainty- their employees can now seamlessly and confidently upgrade to the newest Apple operating system (iOS and macOS) releases and reap the benefits of their advancements without fear of disruption or potential incompatibility.

Disruption-Free

Usage Readiness

Enterprises can now transition to latest Apple products without being hindered by downtimes, prolonged transition layovers or vulnerabilities, thereby unlocking the full potential of Apple’s latest releases from day one. This saves valuable time and effort for their IT teams with no last-minute troubleshooting and reactive fixes.

Seamless

Transition to Latest Operating System

: Enterprises can now confidently upgrade and reap the benefits of the advancements in the latest Apple operating system (iOS and macOS) releases without the fear of disruption or potential incompatibility.

Enhanced Security Profile

: Zero Day Support ensures that every new Apple Operating System is secured against emerging threats right from launch. By eliminating the gap between release and enterprise readiness, Zscaler ensured that its customer’s data, applications and workforce are well-protected.

Reliable and High-Performance User Experience

: Extensive testing as a part of journey towards achieving Zero Day Support which validates compatibility, app performance and seamless access has paved way for its customer’s end users to enjoy uninterrupted connectivity irrespective of whether they connect from a corporate network or work remotely.

Thus, organizations can now adopt Apple’s innovations at full speed without risk, compromise or delay- powered by Zscaler’s unwavering commitment towards Zero-Day Compatibility with Apple Products.

A summary of key outcome drivers for Zscaler Customers as a result of Zscaler achieving Apple Zero Day Compatibility has been captured in the following illustration:

Zscaler’s Apple Zero Day Support Journey: Seamless from Beta to GA:

Zscaler’s achievement of Apple Zero Day Support underscores its proactive approach in ensuring its flagship endpoint security solution is ready the moment Apple makes its latest operating systems available.

This achievement highlights Zscaler’s proactive approach to product readiness. Well ahead of the official launch, Zscaler conducted extensive

beta testing on Apple’s pre-release versions of macOS Tahoe and iOS 26

to

validate

seamless compatibility and functionality

. Each new beta build was systematically validated, and results were published promptly in lockstep with Apple’s rollout to keep our customers informed. Similarly, following Apple’s GA release, our teams carried out the final validation and are

pleased to announce full compatibility with both macOS Tahoe and iOS 26.

With this effort, Zscaler once again demonstrates our commitment to providing zero-day support for the Apple ecosystem, giving customers assurance that their users remain secure and connected when upgrading to the latest operating systems.

Encountering Issues: How to report it?

If you encounter any issues while using Zscaler Client Connector on macOS Tahoe or iOS 26, report them directly to Zscaler Support by raising a Zscaler Support ticket in the Zscaler Customer Portal. It would get addressed through the standard support process.

## Zscaler-Apple ZDS Initiative: We Welcome Your Valuable Collaboration!

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/Articles/aSmPJ00000GeRrV0AV/zscalerapple-zds-initiative-we-welcome-your-valuable-collaboration
- Type: Article
- Last activity: 2026-05-18T14:49:09.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Article Details

Client Connector

DEEPAK G

(Employee) posted an Article

Edited May 18, 2026 at 2:49 PM

Zscaler-Apple ZDS Initiative: We Welcome Your Valuable Collaboration!

About Zscaler’s Zero-Day Support (ZDS) for Apple Ecosystem:

In today’s fast-moving digital era, staying ahead of technological upgrades is no longer optional, it’s essential. With Apple annually releasing new hardware and software offerings across iOS, iPadOS, and macOS, enterprises face twin challenges of adopting these advancements without disruption and ensuring security.

Zscaler’s Zero-Day Support (ZDS) for Apple helps enterprises adopt new Apple releases seamlessly and securely, with an enterprise-ready posture from day one.

In September 2025,

Zscaler achieved zero-day compatibility

with Apple’s newly released macOS and iOS GA product versions, ensuring that the latest supported Zscaler Client Connector releases were compatible the moment these new Apple product versions went live.

Our commitment doesn’t end there. Zscaler’s ongoing ZDS and proactive quality-assurance efforts continue well beyond go-live to maintain reliability and protection as updates evolve.

This presents a great opportunity for you, as a valued Zscaler customer, to get involved. We also publish post‑build test results for Apple Seed and RC releases that you can review to track readiness ahead of GA. Zscaler encourages you to partner with us in testing the compatibility of Zscaler Client Connector with the latest beta releases of macOS and iOS, and share your findings/feedback in our Apple ZDS Corner (a dedicated Zscaler Zenith Community forum for ZDS Q&A and assistance).

How to access the Zscaler-Apple ZDS Corner:

Become a member of the Zenith Community to access the Apple ZDS Corner!

Register or login

here

Navigate to the Apple ZDS Corner:

If you face any challenges in accessing the Apple ZDS Corner, send an email to

community@zscaler.com

Review the Zscaler collaboration and beta testing articles in the Apple ZDS Corner.

Share your findings via article comments or post your own with the ‘Start a conversion’ feature.

Zscaler Product Management & Engineering may request you to share your findings on beta IOS and MacOS securely. Towards this, you can request assistance from your Technical Success Manager (TSM) to open an internal ticket on your behalf, state OS seed version and share the requested logs.

Additionally, if you have a ticket with Apple (Radar or AppleCare Enterprise), please let Zscaler know of the same.

While the Zscaler Product Management & Engineering team will be monitoring the activity, you can monitor it as well by opting-in to ‘Allow Notifications’ on the Apple Zero Day Support activity page.

How to get involved in the Zscaler-Apple ZDS Initiative:

If you are a Zscaler Customer and if you encounter any issues while using Zscaler Client Connector (ZCC) or ZDX or ZDLP on the

GA versions

New sessions available: Register for the EDU-100 workshop

Zenith Community, we’ve just released a new no-cost offering on Zscaler Cyber Academy: Introduction to Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange (EDU‑100) Workshop.

If you’re looking for an accelerated, practical foundation you can apply on the job, this scenario-driven workshop builds task-based competency across core workflows in:

Zscaler Client Connector (ZCC)

Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA)

Zscaler Private Access (ZPA)

Zscaler Digital Experience (ZDX)

Simulations and exploration of a Zscaler lab tenant

Course overview

Introduction to Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange (EDU‑100) Workshop is designed to help you build minimum viable operational competency through guided, hands-on simulations aligned to a targeted subset of EDU‑200 lab activities.

What makes it different is the delivery: you can practice key workflows during and after the session without requiring an individual customer lab tenant, making it easier to build confidence and keep momentum.

## Use SIPA, App Profile bypasses, or ZIA for non-ZPA protocol management.

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/Guides/aSoPJ0000005s1N0AQ/use-sipa-app-profile-bypasses-or-zia-for-nonzpa-protocol-management
- Type: Guide
- Last activity: 2026-02-19T16:15:11.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Guide Details

Technical Guides

27272a

Ben_Garrison

(Employee) posted a Guide

February 19, 2026 at 4:15 PM

Use SIPA, App Profile bypasses, or ZIA for non-ZPA protocol management.

What are the best practices for managing applications that rely on protocols and ports not supported by ZPA?

ZPA is designed primarily for client-to-app, TCP/UDP application access using a brokered, zero-trust architecture. Some applications/protocols need special application-layer handling, peer-to-peer communication, or ultra-low-latency real-time streams, and those can be a poor fit for standard ZPA app segments.

Common protocols/workflows that can be problematic (and why)

Protocol / App type

Typical use

Why it’s challenging with ZPA

SIP

VoIP call setup/control

Requires Application Layer Gateway (ALG) capabilities for controlling and synchronizing connections, which ZPA does not provide

RTP (often with SIP)

Frequently used alongside SIP for audio and video data delivery.

Highly sensitive to latency/jitter/packet loss; real-time streams can degrade when routed through service edges

H.323 / H.248

Legacy voice/video signaling

Complex flows and timing-sensitive behavior

Legacy VoIP softphones

Cisco IP Communicator, older softphones

Commonly depend on SIP/RTP behavior and “directness” of media paths

TFTP

Lightweight config transfers

Simplicity + flow handling expectations can cause reliability issues depending on implementation

What to do instead?

1) Decide early: “ZPA app segment” vs “needs a different path”

Before spending cycles tuning, confirm whether the application requires:

Peer-to-peer client-to-client flows

Dynamic port negotiation / embedded addressing in payloads

Real-time media that degrades with jitter/latency

If yes, treat it as a design decision, not a troubleshooting exercise.

2) Use ZPA VPN for Legacy Apps where it fits

If your use case is “this is effectively a VPN-style app requirement,” ZPA’s VPN for Legacy Apps (formerly Legacy Apps / Legacy SKU) may be the right tool because it supports:

Layer 3-style connectivity patterns for apps that don’t behave like clean client-to-server flows

Routing models that better accommodate legacy protocol expectations (within supported regions/capabilities)

3) Implement bypass rules for ultra-low-latency / real-time traffic

For traffic that must remain extremely latency/jitter-sensitive (common with SIP/RTP), a practical pattern is:

Bypass ZPA for the specific destination(s) and route via an alternate approved path (traditional VPN, SD-WAN breakout, direct internet/ISP path, etc.)

Scope bypass tightly using FQDNs and/or IPs and document why it exists

4) Prefer modernization: move legacy voice/video to UCaaS

When possible, migrating to Teams / Zoom / Webex (UCaaS) reduces the “protocol fit” problem because these platforms are built for modern cloud routing and typically behave better under zero-trust connectivity models.

5) Validate with evidence: PCAPs + flow mapping (not guesswork)

When users report “it connects but audio drops,” or “registers but no media,” focus on:

Control path vs media path (are both reachable?)

One-way audio indicators (routing/NAT asymmetry)

Jitter/packet-loss measurements during peak times

Vendor documentation for required ports/flows (and whether they’re static vs negotiated)

6) Treat it as architecture, not an exception: document and operationalize

When an app can’t be cleanly supported via standard ZPA app access, create a short internal standard that answers:

What apps fall into “legacy/real-time/peer-to-peer” category?

Which approved connectivity patterns exist (VPN for Legacy Apps, bypass + alt path, modernization roadmap)?

Who approves bypass and how it’s reviewed/expired

## How does DNS work with Z-Tunnel 2.0?

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/Guides/aSoPJ00000064s90AA/how-does-dns-work-with-ztunnel-20
- Type: Guide
- Last activity: 2026-03-06T20:26:33.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Guide Details

Technical Guides

Yashraj Singha

(Employee) posted a Guide

Edited March 6, 2026 at 8:26 PM

How does DNS work with Z-Tunnel 2.0?

Note:

Special thanks to

Mohammed Sakr

for their contributions to this guide. If you require help with the implementation of your specific configuration, please contact our

Zscaler Deployment Services team for assistance.

________________________________________________________________________________________

Overview:

Understanding how the Domain Name System (DNS) functions within Z-Tunnel 2.0 is essential for managing how your traffic is routed through the network. In this tunnel mode, Zscaler Client Connector (ZCC) makes forwarding decisions based on your specific profile settings and the Internet Protocol (IP) address of your DNS server.

For Z-Tunnel 2.0, DNS handling is determined by these three Zscaler Client Connector (ZCC) settings:

IP Inclusions/Exclusions

Domain Inclusions/Exclusions

Prioritize DNS Exclusions over Z-Tunnel 2.0

Forwarding logic by DNS server type:

DNS server IP address is private:

By default, private IP ranges are in IP Exclusions.

When the DNS server IP is excluded, Domain Inclusions/Exclusions are evaluated. In this case, only domains that match Domain Inclusions are sent to Zscaler; all other DNS queries follow the local DNS path.

DNS Server IP address is public and not in IP Exclusions:

If the DNS server IP is public and not excluded, all DNS traffic is sent to Zscaler. In this scenario, Domain Inclusions/Exclusions are not evaluated.

DNS server IP is public and is in IP Exclusions:

If the DNS server IP is public but explicitly added to IP Exclusions, Domain Inclusions/Exclusions are evaluated (similar to the private IP case).

mail

Note

: With ZCC 4.1 and above, while sending the DNS traffic to Zscaler, DNS queries are resolved by Global ZEN IP Addresses such as

185.46.212.88

, as illustrated below:

Refer to the documentation

Configuring Zscaler Client Connector Profiles

for more details.

Please reach out to us in the comments section if you have any questions.

## Restrict user logins to Zscaler Client Connector on Android mobile devices

- Last activity: 2026-03-10T13:57:07.000Z

Guide Details

Technical Guides

Yashraj Singha

(Employee) posted a Guide

Edited March 10, 2026 at 1:57 PM

Restrict user logins to Zscaler Client Connector on Android mobile devices

Note:

Special thanks to

Pranjul Karmele

for their contributions to this guide. If you require help with the implementation of your specific configuration, please contact our

Zscaler Deployment Services team for assistance.

________________________________________________________________________________________

Introduction:

Restricting how users log in to the Zscaler Client Connector (ZCC) on Android devices ensures that only devices meeting your organization’s security requirements can access your services. By configuring device postures and groups within the Zscaler Client Connector Portal, you can maintain a reliable and secure environment for your mobile users.

Solution:

Pre-requisites:

Ensure "Device Groups" are enabled for the user's tenant.

Ensure the users are running on ZCC version 3.9 or higher.

Restricting logins for Android devices:

You can restrict user logins to Zscaler Client Connector on Android devices by following these steps:

Log in to the

Zscaler Client Connector Portal

Go to

Administration

Device Postures

Add Device Posture

. Configure the posture profile for Android based on your organization's requirements.

Go to

Administration

Device Groups

and click

Add Device Group

. Select

Android

under the

Platform

section.

Go to Administration >

Platform Settings

, select Android, and enable the

Use Device Groups in Service Entitlement

option.

Go to

Administration

Zscaler Service Entitlement

Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA)

and perform the following:

Enable the

Device Groups

option and select the device group you created in the step above.

Enable

Logout Zscaler Client Connector

when ZIA Entitlement is Enabled

Go to

App Profile

Android

and edit the relevant app profile. Select the

Device Group

you configured earlier.

Now try to login to the ZCC Application on the Android device. You should get the following error:

Once these settings are applied, users attempting to log in to the ZCC application on an unauthorized Android phone will receive an error message indicating that their access is restricted.

To learn more about these features, refer to the documentation

About Device Posture Profiles

and

About Device Groups

## Configure ZCC to use Z Tunnel 1.0 & 2.0 with different proxy gateways

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/Guides/aSoPJ00000068nh0AA/configure-zcc-to-use-z-tunnel-10-20-with-different-proxy-gateways
- Type: Guide
- Last activity: 2026-05-06T11:51:51.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Guide Details

Technical Guides

Yashraj Singha

(Employee) posted a Guide

Edited May 6, 2026 at 11:51 AM

Configure ZCC to use Z Tunnel 1.0 & 2.0 with different proxy gateways

Note:

Special thanks to

Venkatesh Sekar

for their contributions to this guide. If you require help with the implementation of your specific configuration, please contact our

Zscaler Deployment Services team for assistance

________________________________________________________________________________________

Introduction

Zscaler recommends using hybrid mode in Zscaler Client Connector (ZCC) to forward traffic. You can configure ZCC to use both Z-Tunnel 1.0 and Z-Tunnel 2.0 to provide better overall performance. This configuration allows you to use either the same gateway or two different proxy gateways for the tunnels.

Solution

Configuring the forwarding profile

You can set an expression in your forwarding profile to route specific traffic to different nodes. As an example, you can configure the profile to send traffic from Singapore in the following ways:

Route non-standard port traffic to public nodes.

Forward standard port traffic to customer private nodes.

Example Expression is to send the Traffic from the country of Singapore, non-standard port traffic to public nodes, standard port traffic forward to customer Private ZEN Nodes

Application Profile configuration

var country = "${COUNTRY}";

var tunnel2 = "${ZT2_REQUEST}";

if ((shExpMatch(country,"Singapore")) && (tunnel2 == "true")) {

return "PROXY ${GATEWAY}:80; PROXY ${SECONDARY_GATEWAY}:80; DIRECT";

if (shExpMatch(country,"Singapore")) {

return "PROXY :443; PROXY :443;DIRECT";

return "PROXY ${GATEWAY}:80; PROXY ${SECONDARY_GATEWAY}:80; DIRECT";

Please reach out to us in the comments section if you have any questions.

Working of ZCC Listening Proxy & Z-Tunnel 2.0

Note:

Special thanks to

Jaya Aggarwal

and

Venkatesh Sekar

for their contributions to this guide. If you require help with the implementation of your specific configuration, please contact our

Zscaler Deployment Services team for assistance

________________________________________________________________________________________

Introduction

You can configure specific forwarding features in Zscaler Client Connector (ZCC) to control how your web traffic is processed and tunneled. This article explains how the Redirect Web Traffic to Zscaler Client Connector Listening Proxy and Use Z-Tunnel 2.0 for Proxied Web Traffic features work and how they interact with your proxy auto-configuration (PAC) files.

Redirect Web Traffic to Zscaler Client Connector Listening Proxy Option

If you enable the Redirect Web Traffic to Zscaler Client Connector Listening Proxy option, all port 80/443 traffic (from both proxy-aware and non-proxy-aware applications) is intercepted at the LWF/TAP Driver level. The traffic is then redirected to the Zscaler Client Connector (ZCC) TCP Listening Proxy port (port 9000), similar to how Z-Tunnel 1.0 operates.

Decision on Traffic:

By enabling the above option, ZCC reads the SNI (Server Name Indication) from the "client hello" message to determine whether to bypass the traffic or process it.

Need for Forwarding PAC File:

In most cases, a Forwarding PAC file is no longer necessary.

Ideal for Standard Web Traffic:

This setup is well-suited for standard web traffic, as it eliminates the need for maintaining two PAC files.

Only a single App Profile PAC file is required to determine how traffic should be forwarded.

Exception for non-standard Port Traffic:

However, when this option is enabled, the ZCC only redirects 80 and 443 traffic.

The non-standard port traffic is not automatically redirected and must be handled explicitly.

To handle non-standard traffic, it needs to be specified in both the Forwarding PAC and the App Profile PAC files.

Use Z-Tunnel 2.0 for Proxied Web Traffic Option

Web Traffic Tunneling:

This feature tunnels all web traffic (port 80/443) received by the ZCC Listening Ports using Z-Tunnel 2.0.

Default Proxy Statement Behavior:

ZCC sends traffic via Z-Tunnel 2.0 only when transactions match the default proxy statement of the App Profile.

Specific Proxy Statements:

If there is a specific statement redirecting traffic to another proxy or directly (DIRECT), this specific statement takes priority over the default tunneling behavior.

In such cases:

Traffic is sent via Z-Tunnel 1.0.

Alternatively, the traffic is sent DIRECT if bypassed

Additional Reference:

Refer to the documentation

Configuring Forwarding Profiles for Zscaler Client Connector

for more details.

Reviewing use cases for forwarding modes

## ZCC - VPN Interoperability Best Practices

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/Guides/aSoPJ0000006R3x0AE/zcc-vpn-interoperability-best-practices

- Last activity: 2026-07-03T12:44:37.000Z

Guide Details

Technical Guides

Yashraj Singha

(Employee) posted a Guide

Edited July 3, 2026 at 12:44 PM

ZCC - VPN Interoperability Best Practices

Note:

Special thanks to

Akash B

for their contributions to this guide. If you require help with the implementation of your specific configuration, please contact our

Zscaler Deployment Services team for assistance

________________________________________________________________________________________

Introduction

When you configure Zscaler Client Connector (ZCC) to work alongside your Virtual Private Network (VPN), it is important to follow specific interoperability best practices. Proper configuration ensures that your users experience seamless application access without unnecessary latency or routing conflicts.

You should always bypass the VPN peer Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN) from ZCC. This configuration allows the VPN tunnel to establish directly with the endpoint, rather than attempting to route through the proxy.

Managing split tunnel configurations

Depending on your forwarding mode, you must adjust your bypass settings to prevent traffic interception issues and routing conflicts.

Packet filter-based forwarding (Tunnel Mode)

When you use tunnel mode with packet filter-based forwarding, ZCC intercepts traffic at the driver level and does not rely on machine routes. You should keep these best practices in mind for this mode:

Bypass VPN-bound destinations in ZCC.

Remember that if you do not bypass these destinations, ZCC intercepts and encrypts the traffic instead of allowing it to follow your VPN routes.

Route mode traffic forwarding

In route mode, machine routes steer traffic to ZCC. You must consider these guidelines when using route mode:

Do not bypass VPN-bound traffic in ZCC.

Be aware that bypassing this traffic creates conflicting routes and sends traffic to the default gateway, which ultimately breaks application access.

Managing full tunnel configurations

In a full tunnel setup, the VPN installs a default route that sends all traffic into the tunnel. You can choose one of these two recommended approaches:

Set ZCC to Disabled.

Allow all Zscaler Hub IP addresses in the VPN destination list so that Zscaler traffic can successfully reach the cloud.

Note:

Allowing Zscaler Hub IPs while keeping ZCC Enabled can introduce latency, because traffic goes from the VPN to the egress site before reaching the Zscaler cloud. This setup is generally not recommended and should only be used if it is absolutely necessary.

Please reach out to us in the comments if you have any questions.

Guide Details

Technical Guides

Yashraj Singha

(Employee) posted a Guide

Edited July 23, 2026 at 10:39 AM

Generating a new CSR for Enrollment Certificates & Enroll App Connectors in ZPA

Note:

Special thanks to

Subhrajit Mahi

for their contributions to this guide. If you require help with the implementation of your specific configuration, please contact our

Zscaler Deployment Services team for assistance

________________________________________________________________________________________

Introduction

This article walks you through the end-to-end process of generating a new Certificate Signing Request (CSR) for enrollment certificates in Zscaler Private Access (ZPA), signing it with an internal certificate authority (CA), creating an intermediate CA, and configuring App Connector groups and provisioning keys with the new certificate. It also covers re-enrolling existing App Connectors with the newly configured provisioning key.

Solution

Generating a new CSR

Go to Configuration & Control > Certificate Management > Enrollment Certificates.

Click Create CSR. The Create CSR window appears.

In the Create CSR window, enter the following:

Name: Enter a name. Allowed characters include periods (.), hyphens (-), and underscores (_). Other special characters are not allowed.

Description: (Optional)

Click Create to generate the CSR content.

Sign the CSR using your organization's signing CA (root or intermediate CA). This produces the signed certificate.

Proceed to upload the signed certificate.

Reference:

Creating Certificate Signing Requests for Enrollment (CA) Certificates

Uploading Signed CA Certificates

Before uploading, make sure you have the certificate chain associated with your CA certificates ready.

In the Enrollment Certificates table, locate the Certificate Pending icon next to the certificate name and click the Edit icon. The Upload Signed Certificate window appears.

In the Upload Signed Certificate window, enter the following:

Name: Enter a name for the signed certificate. Allowed characters include periods (.), hyphens (-), and underscores (_).

Description: (Optional)

Certificate Signing Request: The CSR text is displayed here.

Certificate: Click Select File and navigate to the signed CA certificate (i.e., the .pem file).

Click Upload. After uploading the signed CA certificate, click the Edit icon in the table again and verify that the Client Certificate Type option is set correctly. This option specifies how the signed CA certificate is used:

Select Client Connector if you are using the enrollment CA certificate for Zscaler Client Connector.

Select Isolation Client if you are using the enrollment CA certificate for Zero Trust Browser clients.

Select None if you are using the enrollment CA certificate for App Connectors and Private Service Edges.

Note: You can either use the uploaded certificate directly to enroll the App Connector, or use it to generate an intermediate certificate for App Connector enrollment. The following steps demonstrate generating an intermediate certificate for App Connector enrollment.

Reference:

Uploading Enrollment (CA) Certificates and the Certificate Chain

Creating an Intermediate CA for App Connector Enrollment

Go to Configuration & Control > Certificate Management > Enrollment Certificates.

Click Generate Certificate.

Configure the following:

Name: Provide a descriptive name.

Type: Select Intermediate CA.

Parent Certificate: Select the previously generated root CA.

Client Certificate Type: Select Client Connector.

Click Create or Save. Your enrollment certificate is now ready for use.

Creating a New App Connector Group

Go to Configuration & Control > Private Infrastructure > App Connector Groups.

Click Add. The Add App Connector Provisioning Keys page appears.

Configure the following:

Name: Enter a name. The same character rules apply as described previously.

Status: Select Enabled.

Signing Certificate: Select the intermediate CA certificate you created in the previous section.

Click Save.

Reference:

Configuring App Connector Groups

Creating a New App Connector Provisioning Key

Go to Configuration & Control > Private Infrastructure > App Connector Keys.

Click Add. The Add App Connector Provisioning Keys page appears.

Configure the following:

Group: Select the App Connector group you created in the previous section.

Name: Provide a name. The same character rules apply as described previously.

Maximum Reuse of Provisioning Key: Set the reuse count based on your deployment plan.

Signing Certificate: Select the enrollment certificate you created in the Creating an Intermediate CA for App Connector Enrollment section.

Click Save.

Reference:

Configuring App Connector Provisioning Keys

Re-enrolling App Connectors

If you want to use existing App Connectors with your own custom enrollment certificate, you have two options:

Option A: Re-provision using the new provisioning key, following the re-provisioning procedure.

Option B: Deploy new App Connectors using the standard provisioning workflow and apply the new provisioning key.

Reference:

Configuring App Connectors

Sources

Understanding Certificates | Zscaler

Creating Certificate Signing Requests for Enrollment (CA) Certificates | Zscaler

Uploading Enrollment (CA) Certificates and the Certificate Chain | Zscaler

Configuring App Connector Groups | Zscaler

Configuring App Connector Provisioning Keys | Zscaler

Configuring App Connectors | Zscaler

Yashraj Singha

Edited 23h ago

Launching Zscaler Client Connector when the UI is inaccessible

Note:

Special thanks to

Karan Kumar

for their contributions to this guide. If you require help with the implementation of your specific configuration, please contact our

Zscaler Deployment Services team for assistance

________________________________________________________________________________________

Introduction

In some scenarios, users may be unable to launch the Zscaler Client Connector (ZCC) through the Start Menu, Desktop shortcut, or System Tray. This can occur while troubleshooting a device where the standard UI entry points are unavailable, even though the ZCC installation and services are present. If the ZCC application is installed, the UI can be launched directly by executing the ZSATray.exe application from the Command Prompt.

Solution

Press Windows + R, type cmd, and click OK.

Navigate to the ZCC tray application directory by running the following command:

cd "C:\Program Files\Zscaler\ZSATray"

Launch the ZCC user interface by executing this command:

ZSATray.exe

Alternatively, the executable can be launched directly using this command:

C:\Program Files\Zscaler\ZSATray\ZSATray.exe

Verify that the Zscaler Client Connector window opens successfully.

Please reach out to us in the comments if you have any questions.

Yashraj Singha

(Employee) posted a Guide

Edited 2h ago

Using Postman API to Fetch Active Enrolled Devices from ZCC Mobile Admin Portal

Note:

Special thanks to

Awin Raj

for their contributions to this guide. If you require help with the implementation of your specific configuration, please contact our

Zscaler Deployment Services team for assistance

____________________________________________________________________________________________

Introduction

Customers need to retrieve a list of active enrolled devices from the Zscaler Client Connector (ZCC) Mobile Admin Portal without logging into the portal directly. They require programmatic access — typically for documentation, auditing, or automation purposes — and want to use API calls via Postman to fetch this data.

The ZCC Mobile Admin Portal exposes a public API that supports fetching enrolled device data. To use this API, customers must first authenticate and obtain a JSON Web Token (JWT), which is then used to authorize subsequent API requests. Many customers are unfamiliar with the required API configuration steps in Postman.

Solution

Please find below the steps to initiate the API call using Postman API to Mobile admin portal and fetch the list of enrolled users -

Authenticating to Zscaler Using the API

Set the Method as POST and URL as

https://mobileadmin.net/papi/auth/v1/login

. For example, if the cloud name is zscloud the URL will be

https://mobileadmin.zscloud.net/papi/auth/v1/login

Click on Headers and add the headers and their corresponding values.

Accept with value as */*

Content-Type with value as "application/json"

Click on Body and configure the body in the format below:

"apiKey": "string",

"secretKey": "string"

Here, apiKey= Client ID, secretKey= Client Secret. We get this from the Client Connector portal.

Click on "Save" to save the configuration and Click "send"

This will display the JWT-Token in the body to be used in other API calls.

Fetching the Device List Using the API

Add another API call of type GET and configure the URL as "

https://api-mobile.zscalerbeta.net/papi/public/v1/downloadServiceStatus?registrationTypes=0

".

Add a Header by the key of auth-token and add the JWT-Token as Value.

Click on Save to save the API call and click on Send. This fetches a list of the Enrolled devices:

Note:

You can filter the list of devices by registration types or states. The following values represent different device states:

0 - All states except Removed

1 - Registered

3 - Removal pending

4 - Unregistered

5 - Removed

6 - Quarantined

In the above example, the registrationTypes has been used as "0", because we needed a list of devices with " All states except Removed".

## Checking Zscaler Client Connector Logs for Split VPN & Trusted Network Detection

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/Guides/aSoPJ0000006ZJF0A2/checking-zscaler-client-connector-logs-for-split-vpn-trusted-network-detection
- Type: Guide
- Last activity: 2026-07-29T19:19:19.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Guide Details

Technical Guides

Yashraj Singha

(Employee) posted a Guide

Edited 4h ago

Checking Zscaler Client Connector Logs for Split VPN & Trusted Network Detection

Note:

Special thanks to

Erick Cruz León

for their contributions to this guide. If you require help with the implementation of your specific configuration, please contact our

Zscaler Deployment Services team for assistance

____________________________________________________________________________________________

Introduction

This guide explains how to verify in Zscaler Client Connector (ZCC) logs that ZCC has detected a Cisco AnyConnect Split VPN connection and that the VPN connection matches a configured Trusted Network Criteria.

Prerequisites:

This scenario applies to Windows endpoints where:

1. Zscaler Client Connector (ZCC) is installed

2. Cisco AnyConnect is installed and used as a Split VPN

3. The customer has configured Trusted Network Criteria based on values provided by the VPN connection, such as DNS servers

In the example below, the Trusted Network Criteria is configured in the Forwarding Profile to match the VPN DNS servers 1.1.1.1 and 1.0.0.1:

Also, the "Evaluate Trusted NW against All Default Route Adapters" and "Enable Split VPN-Trusted Network" are enabled in the Forwarding Profile configuration.

The objective of this procedure is to confirm the following sequence in the logs:

The endpoint is initially detected as NON_TRUSTED

Cisco AnyConnect VPN connects

ZCC detects the VPN adapter

ZCC evaluates Trusted Network Criteria

The configured criteria matches the VPN-provided values

The network state changes to TRUSTED_VPN

ZCC continues enforcing the tunnel in TRUSTED_VPN mode

Key validation requirement:

Make sure to collect the following from the user:

The exact time the user connected to Cisco AnyConnect VPN client

A ZCC debug log bundle with the packet capture

Output of ipconfig /all taken before and the after VPN connection

This information helps correlate:

VPN establishment

Adapter detection

Trusted network evaluation

DNS values pushed by the VPN

Troubleshooting Workflow:

Confirm the initial network state before VPN connection

Before the user connects to Cisco AnyConnect, verify that ZCC is showing the device as NON_TRUSTED.

Example ZCC log entry

2026-06-24 18:39:27.474529(-0600)[9224:11672] DBG ZApp Status: getCurrentNetworkType:NON_TRUSTED getSmeProxyState:TUNNEL_FORWARDING T2State: [ZT2A::SME: 205.220.27.69:443 Protocol: TLS Status: UP Tx: 310 Rx: 245 SNISuffix: zscalertwo.net]

Interpretation:

This confirms that, prior to VPN connection:

The device is currently classified as NON_TRUSTED (Off Trusted) network

ZCC Tunnel Forwarding is in active state

No trusted VPN criteria has yet been matched

Identify the VPN connection event

The user then connects to the Cisco AnyConnect VPN. In this example, the VPN server IP address is: 10.66.108.20

From the packet capture, confirm the connection towards the VPN server at the timestamp provided by the user:

Note: This timestamp becomes the anchor point for searching the ZCC logs. Most of the relevant entries should appear immediately after the VPN is established.

Verify that ZCC Detects the VPN Adapter

Search the ZCC logs using the keywords:

VPN

and

Vpn detected

Expected behavior:

Vpn detected: 1 = VPN detected

Vpn detected: 0 = VPN not detected

Example ZCC log entries:

2026-06-24 18:39:28.034425(-0600)[9224:3768] INF Checking VPN for Adapter Index: 8, checkDescription: 1

2026-06-24 18:39:28.035214(-0600)[9224:3768] DBG Checking VPN for: Cisco AnyConnect Virtual Miniport Adapter for Windows x64

2026-06-24 18:39:28.035214(-0600)[9224:3768] DBG Adapter Operational: 1

2026-06-24 18:39:28.035214(-0600)[9224:3768] INF Vpn detected: 1

Interpretation:

These entries confirm that:

ZCC is enumerating network adapters

The Cisco AnyConnect Virtual Miniport Adapter for Windows x64 has been identified

The adapter is operational

ZCC positively flags the adapter as a VPN interface

Verify Trusted Network Detection after VPN connection

After the VPN adapter is detected, ZCC evaluates the configured Trusted Network Criteria.

Search the logs using the keywords:

detectCurrentNetworkType

evaluateTrustedNetwork

matchDnsServers

Example ZCC log entries:

2026-06-24 18:39:28.038977(-0600)[9224:3768] DBG detectCurrentNetworkType Multiple trusted network enabled!

2026-06-24 18:39:28.038977(-0600)[9224:3768] INF detectCurrentNetworkType Trusted network Name: VPN-DNS, GUID:cdc65b49-61de-432c-91c5-075ffdd58d51

2026-06-24 18:39:28.038977(-0600)[9224:3768] INF matchDnsServers Checking OnNet dns servers

2026-06-24 18:39:28.038977(-0600)[9224:3768] INF matchDnsServers OnNet dns server matched: 1.1.1.1

2026-06-24 18:39:28.038977(-0600)[9224:3768] DBG evaluateTrustedNetwork On-net detected for ANY condition

2026-06-24 18:39:28.038977(-0600)[9224:3768] INF detectCurrentNetworkType on net criteria matched for network !: VPN-DNS

2026-06-24 18:39:28.038977(-0600)[9224:3768] INF detectCurrentNetworkType zpa is inactive, on net criteria matched for network !: VPN-DNS

2026-06-24 18:39:28.038977(-0600)[9224:3768] INF Skipping evaluation for Split vpn trusted as on net criteria already matched for network.

Interpretation:

These entries show that:

ZCC is evaluating multiple trusted network definitions

The trusted network named VPN-DNS is being assessed

ZCC is checking the endpoint DNS servers

A configured trusted DNS server match was found: 1.1.1.1

The Trusted Network Criteria is successfully matched

Because the endpoint is already determined to be on a trusted network, split VPN trusted evaluation is skipped afterward

Confirm transition to TRUSTED_VPN

Once the criteria is matched, ZCC should transition the network type to TRUSTED_VPN.

Search the logs using the keywords:

TRUSTED_VPN detected

Example ZCC log entries:

2026-06-24 18:39:28.047144(-0600)[9224:3768] DBG [ZSAFW] onLocationChange: Begin. Current Network Type: TRUSTED_VPN

2026-06-24 18:39:28.065926(-0600)[9224:3768] INF TRUSTED_VPN detected

2026-06-24 18:39:28.065926(-0600)[9224:3768] INF Will continue enforcing tunnel in TRUSTED_VPN.

Interpretation:

This confirms that:

ZCC has reclassified the current network as TRUSTED_VPN

The trusted VPN condition was successfully recognized

Tunnel enforcement remains active in TRUSTED_VPN mode

Validate the Network Type in the logs

After the Trusted_VPN network is detected, the ZSATunnel logs should continue to report the device as TRUSTED_VPN

Example log entries:

2026-06-24 18:39:28.994375(-0600)[9224:11672] DBG ZApp Status: getCurrentNetworkType:TRUSTED_VPN getSmeProxyState:TUNNEL_FORWARDING T2State: [ZT2A::SME: 205.220.27.69:443 Protocol: TLS Status: UP Tx: 320 Rx: 245 SNISuffix: zscalertwo.net]

2026-06-24 18:39:56.696151(-0600)[9224:11672] DBG ZApp Status: getCurrentNetworkType:TRUSTED_VPN getSmeProxyState:TUNNEL_FORWARDING T2State: [ZT2B::SME: 170.85.231.69:443 Protocol: DTLS Status: UP Tx: 5 Rx: 4 SNISuffix: zscalertwo.net]

2026-06-24 18:39:59.376531(-0600)[9224:11672] DBG ZApp Status: getCurrentNetworkType:TRUSTED_VPN getSmeProxyState:TUNNEL_FORWARDING T2State: [ZT2A::SME: 104.129.192.15:443 Protocol: DTLS Status: UP Tx: 7 Rx: 5 SNISuffix: zscalertwo.net]

2026-06-24 18:40:12.815821(-0600)[9224:11672] DBG ZApp Status: getCurrentNetworkType:TRUSTED_VPN getSmeProxyState:TUNNEL_FORWARDING T2State: [ZT2A::SME: 104.129.192.15:443 Protocol: DTLS Status: UP Tx: 7 Rx: 5 SNISuffix: zscalertwo.net]

2026-06-24 18:40:20.942541(-0600)[9224:11672] DBG ZApp Status: getCurrentNetworkType:TRUSTED_VPN getSmeProxyState:TUNNEL_FORWARDING T2State: [ZT2A::SME: 104.129.192.15:443 Protocol: DTLS Status: UP Tx: 7 Rx: 5 SNISuffix: zscalertwo.net]

ZCC UI should also show the TRUSTED_VPN as network type

Interpretation:

These entries validate that the network classification remains stable as TRUSTED_VPN after the VPN connection and trusted network match.

Verify DNS Servers Pushed by the VPN

To confirm why the Trusted Network Criteria matched, review the DNS server values in the ZCC debug logs and compare them with the DNS configuration on Windows using the following command in CMD Terminal:

ipconfig /all

Example ZCC log entries:

2026-06-24 18:39:29.902591(-0600)[9224:8848] DBG DNS Servers: 1.1.1.1

2026-06-24 18:39:29.902591(-0600)[9224:8848] DBG DNS Servers: 1.0.0.1

2026-06-24 18:39:29.902591(-0600)[9224:8848] DBG DNS Servers: 192.168.88.1

2026-06-24 18:39:29.902591(-0600)[9224:8848] DBG DNS Servers: 8.8.8.8

Windows CMD Output:

Interpretation:

This confirms that the endpoint is using a combination of:

VPN-pushed DNS servers

Local network DNS servers

In this example, the presence of 1.1.1.1 and 1.0.0.1 matches the configured Trusted Network Criteria, which causes ZCC to classify the connection as TRUSTED_VPN.

Note

: The example in this article uses DNS Servers as the Trusted Network Criteria. However, customers may configure Trusted Network Criteria using other conditions available in the Forwarding Profile, including:

DNS Search Domains

Hostname and IP

Network Range

Default Gateway

DHCP Server

Egress IP

Troubleshooting scenarios and Best Practices:

Confirm the exact Trusted Network Criteria configured

Validate the actual values present on the endpoint after VPN connection

Compare those values against the ZCC debug logs

Confirm that the matched value aligns with the intended trusted network policy

Always confirm the precise VPN connection timestamp

Correlate packet capture, ZCC debug logs, and Windows network configuration

If the VPN should be trusted but no match occurs, verify:

The VPN adapter is operational

The expected DNS servers or other criteria are actually present on the endpoint

The configured Trusted Network Criteria values are correct

When Cisco AnyConnect is used as a Split VPN on Windows, ZCC can detect the VPN adapter and evaluate whether the connection matches a configured Trusted Network Criteria. If the VPN-provided values match the configured trusted conditions, ZCC transitions the device from NON_TRUSTED to TRUSTED_VPN and continues tunnel enforcement accordingly.

The most important troubleshooting artifacts are:

The VPN connection timestamp

ZCC debug logs with packet capture

ZSATunnel logs

Windows DNS configuration

These data points help validate whether ZCC correctly detected both the VPN and the trusted criteria match.

Please reach out to us in the comments if you have any questions.

(Employee): asked a question.

July 7, 2020 at 4:05 AM

Z-App -8 Network Error when users log in on Windows 10

Hello, has anyone experienced the networking error -8 when the app runs on certain versions of windows 10 Enterprise? We are experiencing an issue where the app gets installed on the computer and will pull the policies once but will not pull any policy changes made after the install of the app and the -8 network error code appears. I’ve created a ticket with Zscaler, but none of the techs have given anything that resolves the error on multiple computers. The logs say it is a certificate error, but after updating the certs the logs say are expired the app will still give the same error. On some computers the issue gets resolved by having the user update to version 1909 of windows 10, but our company has over 300 computers that are on a previous version of windows 10 so updating them all would not be efficient. Does anyone have any suggestions on what to try? Is there a known issue with the Z-app running on windows 10 computers that are not on windows 10 version 1909?

Client Connector

11 answers

2.88K views

Top Rated Answers

cburge97

(Customer)

6 years ago

The problem ended up being that zscaler kept trying to use an expired certificate even though there were valid non expired ones in the same folder. Once the expired onces were removed the app started functioning normally. You’d think the app would be smart enough to grab the unexpired certificate that it installs durrinf the install process but I guess thats not the case.

grrttmrtn:

gs showing after you upgrade the ce

Hi Chris,

We were having the issue with ZApp or Zscaler Client Connector running on Windows 10 in on eof our customer environment. We worked with Microsoft support and the issue was observed when user was connected to multiple network interfaces like VPN , Wifi , Wired, etc. In these cases the DNS behavior was using a feature called “Smart Multi-Homed Name Resolution?. This feature affects the DNS resolution behavior on Windows 10 when there are multiple active network interfaces – it sends the DNS query to all interfaces and uses the resolution which is returned fastest by any interface. Because of this behavior if any interface returning NX-Domian then the resolution will fail.

Microsoft Engineer advised to try the below commands(with elevated privileges in power shell) on one of the affected users for testing:

Set-ItemProperty -Path “HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\DNSClient? -Name DisableSmartNameResolution -Value 1 -Type DWord

Set-ItemProperty -Path “HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Dnscache\Parameters? -Name DisableParallelAandAAAA -Value 1 -Type Dword

We had to create the Dword manually in registry for the first command which was not working as the Dword didn’t exist.

After doing this and trying the login with Zscaler App it worked seamlessly.

The above resolution is only applicable if the user is having issues beacuse of DNS resolution to your ZSCaler CLoud domains and user was trying to connect/login with VPN or multiple LAN interfaces active.

Do let us know if this helps.

ZAPP intune deployment

Hello, I am currently trying to deploy ZAPP to our Windows 10 environment using intunes. We are fully cloud environment and use Azure AD for SSO.

I followed following video to push ZAPP to my WIndows users. I can see app is deployed perfectly fine. But only issue I get is it does not do SSO automatically. You can the screen where you have to put your username and then it downloads all the configuration.

I was wondering if there is a way where I can do fully automatic deployment so user does not have to login etc.

Regards

Discourse-expand

mryan

(Employee)

6 years ago

Hi,

If you’re using

admin.zscaler.net

, then --cloudName zscaler would be correct (

admin.zscalertwo.net

would have --cloudName zscalertwo , etc)

the --userDomain should be the domainsuffix you use to authenticate. i.e. if you logon to AzureAD as

bob@thisdomain.com

, then --userDomain

thisdomain.com

would be correct. The domain you logon to Azure AD would also be the same domain you’d enter into the dialog box that Zscaler App presents to you.

Thanks

November 9, 2021 at 8:44 PM

ZCC SSO on VDI instance

Documentation under Supporting Citrix states

"If you are using non-persistent VDIs where users get fresh desktops each time they connect, they will need to re-enroll each time. "

But under " Best Practices for Using Zscaler Client Connector in a VDI" it states

The following conditions apply when using Zscaler Client Connector (formerly Zscaler App or Z App) in a virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI):

Zscaler recommends that you don’t log in to Zscaler Client Connector on the master VM.

To use the

STRICTENFORCEMENT install option

, you must have the

HIDEAPPUIONLAUNCH install option

disabled. This allows Zscaler Client Connector to remind users to enroll with Zscaler Client Connector before accessing the internet.

To use the

USERDOMAIN install option

, you must use Integrated Windows Authentication (IWA).

Does this mean that a user can be automatically logged into ZCC on a non-persistent VDI using strictenforcement and userdomain integrated with IWA?

martinkiska

(Customer)

4 years ago

On Win platform we are facing bad behavior of forwarding profile MTU configuration when people are testing speed via

speedtest.net

, because they use nonstandard port (8080). When nonstandard port is used, then MTU is not correctly propagated and it slows down a lot upload performance - IP fragmentation is happening (in downstream path ZCC is following MTU configuration). Due to that we have many reports that ZCC is slowing down user’s Internet. We are pointing them for example to speedtest.cesnet.cz which is using standard 80/443 ports for testing. We have already ticket opened for that. So just for others to be aware of small details which might have big impact.

Z-tunnel2.0, DTLS, ZCC 3.9.0.160, private service enforcement node.

When public service enforcement node is used then MTU configuration is also not taken into account (default hidden 1400B is used) and if your traffic is being fragmented on some slow ISP box then you might again face slow upload.

## Compare ezAgent and ZCC - when to use which?

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009evlrcCAA/compare-ezagent-and-zcc-when-to-use-which
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-05-31T09:25:22.000Z

Client Connector

hukel

(Customer) to

sfdc

(Employee): asked a question.

January 28, 2021 at 3:42 PM

Compare ezAgent and ZCC - when to use which?

We are evaluating Zscaler and are thinking through our various use cases. Once area that is still fuzzy for me is when/where to use ezAgent for proxy management vs Zscaler Client Connector.

Is there a write-up somewhere that compares these two?

Client Connector

2 answers

704 views

Top Rated Answers

phayes

(Employee)

5 years ago

Hi Hugh,

The Zscaler Client Connector (ZCC) can do everything the eZ Agent can do, and more - eZ Agent availability is more a legacy option for current customers with it already deployed.

As an example of how ZCC is a complete replacement and more - if you need to just configure and enforce proxy settings, ZCC can operate in this mode, but it also can forward all Internet traffic (not just HTTP/HTTPS/FTP), it’s one agent for our entire platform (ZIA/ZPA/ZDX), and supports functionality like network detection, tamper resistance, etc.

Most customers, whether current or new, are deploying the Client Connector to their managed devices but we’ve other options, too, depending on the use-case. If you haven’t had a chance to review it yet, I highly recommend our

Choosing Traffic Forwarding Methods

guide!

Selected as Best

Tunneling Zscaler internal traffic in a "No Default Route" environment

Zscaler Client Connector needs to be able to reach the Zscaler Cloud service to update the application, policy, etc. This can be a challenge in an environment without a Default-Route out to the Internet.

A new ZCC feature allows you to configure an explicit proxy (such as ZIA) for this traffic.

This video walks you through how to set this up.

Video - Tunnel ZCC Traffic

## Z-APP SSL inspection on Android

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009evmSYCAY/zapp-ssl-inspection-on-android
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2025-09-03T12:05:54.000Z

Client Connector

Pspearsjr

(Customer) to

(Employee): asked a question.

August 19, 2020 at 2:37 PM

Z-APP SSL inspection on Android

When we have SSL inspection enabled for Android we find it seems to break most apps on the Android mobile device. The browsers seem to be fine as we push the Zscaler CA from our MDM and we have the Z-APP AKA zscaler client connector checked to install the Zscaler CA. Still many apps lose internet connectivity when Android SSL inspection is enabled. Example apps Garmin Connect, Pandora, Amazon Music and many others. I have confirmed manually the zscaler cert is in the User store and trusted to network and apps. Is there a fix for this or is this issue just due to cert pinning of the Android apps themself? I am wondering if there is possibly a fix to this? We cannot possibly disable ssl inspection for these domain as that would impact our ability to inspect SSL on our windows devices etc. THe only fix I have found is disable SSL inspection for Android in the Z-app settings.

Additionally we tested with ChromeOS and it has this same issue I presume due to it’s android apps.

Client Connector

I think the feature available now. Look Policy > SSL Inspection > Create SSL rule > look for device group

How to get a new IP address?

Hello All, (Reposting since no replies on the other group)

Our users are assigned an IP address from the San Francisco IV block by zApp. We are configured to get one of 512 (?) available addresses and they are randomly assigned to our users when they first visit the internet. This assignment is persistent. (I’ve had the same IP for over three week now).

The problem: one of the IPs assigned to our users is black-flagged due to it being used by a SPAM / BOT.

We use Cloudflare service to protect our website. Every one of our users with the suspicious IP visits our site, they are challenged by a Captcha because Cloudflare considers traffic from this IP “suspicous?. Since the IP is cached for my users, they see the Captcha every time they visit our website. Our business requires them to visit several times a day. So they are challenged several times a day.

Q: Is there a way to get the zApp to assign a new IP to my users (so they are not forced to continue using the problematic IP)?

Thank you,

-tomas

## ZSATray Icon issue client connector

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009evmXECAY/zsatray-icon-issue-client-connector
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-05-31T08:44:58.000Z

Client Connector

PetRu

(Customer) to

sfdc

(Employee): asked a question.

March 11, 2021 at 1:22 PM

ZSATray Icon issue client connector

Hello community,

Some of our colleagues experience an annoying / hindering behavior of the ZCC on their Win 10 clients (1909 or 20H2).

In the mid of January we upgraded successfully couple thousand ZCC installations from 1.5.x to 3.1.x . Around 3-4 weeks later, problems on clients started when users connect to their virtual or physical workstations using Citrix.

The ZCC doesn’t start/connect as usual, the ZSATray.exe process starts and gets stopped within the next second. Just a few seconds later that is repeated, again, again and again … On some clients all ZSATray.exe processes disappear after getting stopped, in some cases couple of them remain as stopped.

Each time a ZSATray.exe process tries to start, it generates a new Zscaler tray icon, which will not automatically disappear when the process is stopped / disappearing.

Result: An whole screen full of Zscaler tray icons when you check the hidden tray icons. Usually they are all gray (like disabled/not connect ZCC), rarely there is a lonely “connected? blue icon, but you cannot open ZCC through any of them (neither gray, nor blue), they disappear as soon as you move the mouse over them.

You can clean up all tray icons, but shortly there start to reappear, one by one.

Due to the frequent attempt to restart the process, a ton of logfiles get generated, over 100k files are easily reached.

We already tried the newer version 3.1.0.129 instead of our .103 we currently use, as upgrade installation as well as clean installation. No success.

As soon as you login via RDP (Remote Desktop User group), it works fine, if the colleagues connect again via Citrix, the issue reappears.

After you logged in once with admin permission via RDP, the issue seems to be solved, also when you login later via Citrix is seem to work fine so far.

But that cannot be the solution, granting admin permission generally to all users and hoping it is solved afterwards – logistical nightmare, especially as we currently only from a few workstations that issue is reported, but potentially couple hundreds could be effected!

We checked the location service settings, but that also wasn’t the solution:

Logging in with one user after activating the location service – ZCC works fine. Next day another user works with the same workstation, the issue appears again.

For that user it helped to perform a cold reboot (Windows > Shutdown > Turn on via power button), for another colleague on another workstation it didn’t work.

So far, everything we tried and eventually worked feels like rolling a dice.

We would appreciate if one of you had similar experiences and a working solution for it or an idea / suggestion what we can check or change to fix it properly.

Thanks!

regards

Client Connector

## Zscaler Client with Split tunnel environnement

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009evmXFCAY/zscaler-client-with-split-tunnel-environnement
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-05-31T08:48:26.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Client Connector

yosr

(Partner) to

sfdc

(Employee): asked a question.

March 8, 2021 at 3:37 PM

Zscaler Client with Split tunnel environnement

Hello,

Below is a description of the problem we encounter:

We have salesforce domains that do source IP filtering so they only accept requests coming from our IPs, so to take into account these ecxeptions we have created bypasses for the salesforce domains on the two pac files FWD pac file + App profile pac file (because we are the ztunnel2.0 version) and we have added in the split tunnel configuration the salesforce domains that will have to go through this split tunnel.

However, we have noticed that there is a local evasion on the user’s computer when he tries to go to salesforce, in fact his request to salesforce arrives with the user’s IP instead of the IP of the VPN gateway, which means that he cannot connect to salesforce.

Someone has a solution for this problem ?

Thanks.

Client Connector

5 answers

1.36K views

tharcourt

(Employee)

5 years ago

Yosr,

There are a few things you can try, but it all depends on the ZCC version you are running, and how you have it configured. Try bypassing the IPs or FQDN (Domain is supported on the latest versions), in the App profile under VPN bypasses. You can also try switching from Route based to Packet Filter, or Vice Versa. This will allow routes to direct the Salesforce IPs to the VPN. If those don’t work, open a support ticket and include the ZCC logs.

Thanks,

-Todd Harcourt-

yosr

(Partner)

5 years ago

Hello Todd,

thank you for your feedback but this is not an option we are considering implementing at the moment.

we just want to bypass zscaler and send salesforce traffic to the VPN tunnel.

Do you have any ideas about the problem we are facing?

Thanks.

tharcourt

(Employee)

5 years ago

Yosr,

Have you considered using the Zscaler Identity Proxy for Salesforce? It will provide better security with less latency than going through VPN and just limiting the access to your IP addresses. Zscaler can provide Access Control by User/Group/Location, Advanced Threat Protection, DLP, File Control, and CASB Functionality (DLP, Malware) as well. The Identity Proxy Feature will ensure all access goes through Zscaler, Is Authenticated first using your IDP, and then Security is applied using SSL decryption and DPI.

Just an Idea,

-Todd Harcourt-

## Bypass ssl inpsection for zscaler domains on the FW

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009evmZWCAY/bypass-ssl-inpsection-for-zscaler-domains-on-the-fw

Client Connector

yosr

(Partner) to

sfdc

(Employee): asked a question.

April 28, 2021 at 7:45 AM

Bypass ssl inpsection for zscaler domains on the FW

Hello,

We have a customer who is using the zscaler clinet connector to forward traffic to Zscaler, also the ZCC is configured with the Ztunnel2.0.

When the customer is on remote he configures a full VPN.

Also the customer choices to desactivate the ssl inspection on Zscaler and to activate it on his internal FW.

So when he activates his full VPN he remarks that the ztunnel on ZCC change from version 2.0 to version 1.0. After investigation we found that the ssl inspection on his internal FW causses this issue. we tried to bypass ssl inepction for zscaler domains definied on

ips.zscaler.net

but the probelm persists.

Have someone already faced this kind of problem ? or do you know which other problems we should bypass ?

PS: The cloud name used is zscalerthree.

Thanks.

Client Connector

4 answers

411 views

yosr

(Partner)

5 years ago

ZSclaer ssl inspection is already disabled, and it’s activated only on the FW side.

yosr

(Partner)

5 years ago

Hello,

Ztunnel 2.0 is using DTLS

Gordon Wright

(Customer)

5 years ago

Is your ztunnel 2.0 using DTLS or TLS?

Gordon Wright

(Customer)

5 years ago

Your firewall is just trying to SSL inspect the ZCC ztunnel and not the encrypted data inside the ztunnel. I don’t think this is the outcome you are trying to achieve.

What’s the problem your are trying to fix that made you disable the Zscaler SSL inspection?

Can a User with multiple devices use them simultaneously whilst logged in using that same single account

Can a User with multiple devices use them simultaneously whilst logged in using that same single account?

Can a User log into their Zscaler Client Connector on one Device using their single user account and also on their other Device with ZCC using the same username?

Client Connector

Michael - You can use multiple devices logged in with the same username at the same time.
